evidence.claim: In Y. lipolytica, complex I deficiency is lethal and is rescued by NDH2 redirected to the matrix side but not by the native external NDH2; the authors conclude that shuttles moving redox equivalents from the matrix to the cytosolic side are insufficient.
evidence.source: Kerscher SJ, Eschemann A, Okun PM, Brandt U. J Cell Sci 2001;114(Pt 21):3915-3921. PMID 11719558
evidence.caveat: Shows insufficiency of matrix-to-cytosol shuttling at complex I-replacing capacity; does not test an ethanol-acetaldehyde shuttle specifically.

evidence.claim: Y. lipolytica is a non-fermenting yeast that neither grows anaerobically nor produces ethanol; ADH1, ADH2 or ADH3 is required for ethanol utilization (eight ADH genes tested).
evidence.source: Gatter M, Ottlik S, Kovesi Z, Bauer B, Matthaus F, Barth G. Fungal Genet Biol 2016;95:30-38. PMID 27486067
evidence.caveat: Full text not opened (paywalled). The ADH1/ADH2/ADH3 to YALI1D33961g/YALI1E21128g/YALI1A16292g mapping is recalled from the task prompt, not verified. The abstract does not report ADH localization.

evidence.claim: In S. cerevisiae, the mitochondrial alcohol dehydrogenase Adh3 runs an ethanol-acetaldehyde redox shuttle that moves matrix NADH to the cytosol (required for respiratory growth of ndi1 mutants).
evidence.source: Bakker BM et al. J Bacteriol 2000;182(17):4730-4737. PMID 10940011, PMC111347
evidence.caveat: Cross-species context for why R132 exists in yeast models; not Y. lipolytica evidence.

evidence.claim: S. cerevisiae Adh3 carries a mitochondrial transit peptide at residues 1-24 (mature chain 25-375).
evidence.source: UniProtKB P07246 (ADH3_YEAST), feature 'Transit peptide 1-24', evidence ECO:0000305 citing PubMed 2188098
evidence.caveat: The task prompt gave a 27-residue presequence string; UniProt annotates 1-24.

evidence.claim: No Adh3-type ortholog with a presequence: YALI1A15227g (R132) and the R130 genes YALI1D33961g, YALI1E21128g, YALI1A16292g are 67.6-71.1 % identical to the mitochondrial ADHs Sc Adh3, Kl ADH3 and Kl ADH4, but their local alignments start at mitochondrial-ADH residue 26-30, so no residue aligns to the transit peptide. For the other eight R132 genes, the best-scoring hit among Sc Adh1-5, Sfa1, Adh6, Adh7, Bdh1 and Kl ADH3/ADH4 is 22.5-31.1 % identical (local alignments of 61-365 columns).
evidence.source: Local Smith-Waterman (Gotoh affine gaps, BLOSUM62, gap open 11 / extend 1), RefSeq and UniProt sequences fetched 2026-10-13

evidence.claim: The only predicted-mitochondrial R132 gene, YALI1F11481g, has no gene-level alcohol dehydrogenase evidence: RefSeq XP_505149.1 and KEGG yli:2908523 name it 'NADPH-dependent alkenal/one oxidoreductase' (MDR superfamily, Pfam PF08240/PF13602); one paper lists YALI0F08129g among 11 BLAST-identified 'putative' ADH genes with no deletion phenotype; another calls it a mitochondrial inner membrane protease without experimental support.
evidence.source: NCBI protein XP_505149.1; KEGG yli:2908523; UniProtKB Q6C2G3; PMC6201493 (Microb Cell Fact 2018); PMC13640256 (Microb Cell Fact 2026)

evidence.claim: The mitochondrial call for YALI1F11481g depends on a 61-residue N-terminal extension present only in the CLIB89 gene model (XP_505149.2, 401 aa). The DNA is identical in CLIB89 and CLIB122; the CLIB122 model (XP_505149.1, 340 aa) starts at the downstream ATG and is predicted non-mitochondrial by all three tools. No gene-specific transcript evidence for the upstream start was found.
evidence.source: NCBI NC_090775.1 and NC_006072.1; XM_505149.3 (provisional RefSeq, 'incomplete on both ends'); Magnan et al. 2016 PLoS ONE 11:e0162363 (PMC5014426), CDS selection 'based on size and RNA-Seq support'

evidence_of_absence_summary: No R132 gene combines ADH evidence with a mitochondrial targeting signal. Y. lipolytica neither produces ethanol nor grows anaerobically, and its matrix-to-cytosol redox shuttles cannot replace complex I. This is indirect evidence; no Y. lipolytica measurement of mitochondrial ADH activity was found or made.
